target.title: fix(media-understanding): apply imageMaxDimensionPx resize to image description input (#101923)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #101923. The image description pre-processing pipeline (`prepareImageDescriptionInput`) passes images through at original dimensions without applying `agents.defaults.imageMaxDimensionPx`. Phone-camera photos (typically 4000×8000) exceed provider limits (Anthropic: 8000px/side, 25MP total) and fail with:

```
Image dimensions exceed the 25,000,000 pixel input limit: 4536x8064
```

This affects `openclaw infer image describe --model ...`, `describeImageFileWithModel`, and `describePreparedImageWithModel` — all three call `prepareImageDescriptionInput` which only converts HEIC→JPEG without any dimension limits.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds a `resizeToJpeg` step after `normalizeImageDescriptionInput` when `imageMaxDimensionPx` is configured. This reuses the same image-ops resize ladder already used by the tool image output sanitizer and web media optimization pipelines.

## Evidence

### Branch prerun (commit 3e38c55)

When `imageMaxDimensionPx` is set:
- Image ≤ limit: passes through unchanged
- Image > limit: downscaled to fit via `resizeToJpeg` (maxSide = configured limit)
- No `imageMaxDimensionPx` configured: behavior unchanged (no resize)

### Before the fix
```
Image dimensions exceed the 25,000,000 pixel input limit: 4536x8064 (36578304 pixels)
```

### After the fix (with `imageMaxDimensionPx: 2000`)
Image is downscaled to ≤ 2000px longest side before the provider call.

## Files Changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/media-understanding/runtime.ts` | `prepareImageDescriptionInput`: +`resizeToJpeg` with `maxSide` from `imageMaxDimensionPx` when configured |
